title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is describing the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}, meaning the stratification of the Deligne–Mumford boundary by the number of double points.

Objects from the previous pages:
- D_d is the normalization of the closed stratum of curves with at least d nodes. A point of D_d is a stable curve together with a chosen set of d of its nodes. D_d is locally immersed in the compactification.
- D_d^! → D_d is the S_d-Galois étale cover that orders the d chosen nodes (equivalently, the branches of the normal-crossings divisor).
- T_d is a rank-d local system of free Z-modules. It is Z^{I_d}, I_d = {1..d}, on D_d^!, descended through S_d. Locally it is the lattice generated by the loops around the d local branches: the vanishing cycles, i.e. the Dehn multitwists.
- G_d = T_d ⊗ G_m is a twisted torus of dimension d.
- P_d is a G_d-torsor on D_d. It is the punctured normal bundle, the product of the d normal line bundles with zero sections removed. T_d is recovered as the H_1 (= π_1) of the fibres of P_d.
- For d ≥ d', D_{d,d'} parametrizes points of D_d together with a d'-element subset of the d nodes. Then D_{d,d'} → D_d is a finite étale cover of degree C(d,d'), and D_{d,d'} → D_{d'} is a local immersion.

This page:
- (193) The two local systems are pulled back to D_{d,d'}: T(d,d')_d of rank d and T(d,d')_{d'} of rank d'.
- (194) There is a canonical surjection T(d,d')_d → T(d,d')_{d'}, called 'tautological'.
- (195) A cartesian diagram identifies D^!_{d,d'} = D^!_d ×_{D_d} D_{d,d'} with the constant scheme over D_d^! of d'-element subsets of I_d. D^!_{d,d'} lies over D_{d,d'} (Galois group of the type S_{d'} × S_{d−d'}) and, by a dashed arrow, over D^!_{d'}. The arrow is dashed presumably because an ordering of the chosen subset must be induced, e.g. from the order of I_d.
- (196) After pullback to D^!_{d,d'}, the tautological map becomes the coordinate projection Z^{I_d} → Z^{J}, |J| = d'.

What it serves: the next page derives from this the smooth epimorphism of tori G(d,d')_d → G(d,d')_{d'}. It then gives the isomorphism P(d,d')_{d'} ≅ P(d,d')_d ∧^{G_d} G_{d'}, saying the torsor of the smaller stratum is induced from the larger one. Transitivity is then checked for triples d ≥ d' ≥ d''. The aim is a coherent system of tori, torsors and fundamental groupoids ΠP_d^* over the boundary strata. That system is a combinatorial-algebraic model of the 'tubular neighbourhood at infinity' that glues the Teichmüller groupoid along the boundary.

In modern terms, T_d with its surjective generization maps is the groupified characteristic (ghost) sheaf M̄^gp of the canonical log structure of the normal-crossings boundary. Locally it is N^d → Z^d, and generization maps are surjective coordinate projections. P_d is the G_m^d-torsor of the corresponding Deligne–Faltings / Borne–Vistoli presentation of that log structure. The fibres (S^1)^d of its real version are the fibres of the Kato–Nakayama space, or real oriented blow-up.
errors: The transcription's 'D^!_{d,d'} = D^!_d ×_{D_d} D_{d'}' should read ×_{D_d} D_{d,d'}. A fibre product over D_d needs an object over D_d, and the cartesian square (195) makes this clear; this is either a slip of the pen or a misreading.

There is a variance subtlety, not an error. Local monodromy inclusions of punctured neighbourhoods give Z^{d'} ↪ Z^d. Grothendieck instead uses the projection Z^d ↠ Z^{d'}, coming from restricting normal-direction torsors. That choice is consistent with the torsor induction (198) on the next page, so the page is internally correct.

ideas.what: Stratification of the DM boundary by number of nodes, with normalized strata D_d, the ordered-branch S_d-covers D_d^!, and the subset-choice covers D_{d,d'}.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of a normal-crossings boundary; dual-graph stratification of M̄_{g,n}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower, but not in this detail

ideas.what: Rank-d local system T_d of loops around the branches, with a canonical surjective 'tautological' map T_d|D_{d,d'} → T_{d'}|D_{d,d'}; locally this is the coordinate projection Z^{I_d} → Z^J.
ideas.modern_name: Groupified characteristic sheaf M̄^gp of the boundary log structure and its generization (cospecialization) maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: K. Kato, Fontaine–Illusie (log structures, c. 1988–89); F. Kato for log smooth curves (2000)

ideas.what: G_d-torsor P_d (punctured normal bundle), with the induced-torsor compatibility P_{d'} ≅ P_d ∧^{G_d} G_{d'} along D_{d,d'}, and fundamental groupoids ΠP_d^* as the 'neighbourhood at infinity'.
ideas.modern_name: Torsor presentation of a log structure (Deligne–Faltings log structure; Borne–Vistoli; Olsson); fibres of the Kato–Nakayama space / real oriented blow-up; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Kato–Nakayama (1999); Borne–Vistoli (2012); Ihara–Nakamura for M_{g,n} at maximal degeneration

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, by hand, the essentials of the logarithmic structure of M̄_{g,ν}. He has the rank-d lattice local systems on strata with surjective generization maps, the associated G_m^d-torsors, and the induced-torsor compatibilities with transitivity for triples d ≥ d' ≥ d''. He uses this as the gluing data for fundamental groupoids at infinity, a precursor of the log/Kato–Nakayama approach to the Teichmüller groupoid.
missed.quote: on a alors un homomorphisme canonique surjectif (dit "tautologique") (194) T(d,d')_d → T(d,d')_{d'} ... s'identifie à l'homomorphisme de projection Z^d → Z^{d'}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck's 'structure à l'infini' programme was formulated in terms that are essentially log-geometric, before Kato and Fontaine–Illusie. That is historically relevant to the log-étale / Kato–Nakayama treatments of profinite and pro-unipotent Teichmüller groupoids (Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki, Ihara). It is a precursor rather than a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carefully and correctly sets up routine combinatorics of boundary strata. Its interest is that it anticipates the characteristic-sheaf and torsor formalism of log geometry, applied to the Teichmüller tower, apparently before that formalism existed. Still, no result here would be new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'symét. local du rang d' should read 'syst. local de rang d' (système local); likewise for rank d'.
The second line of (193) is written in the image as 'T(d*,d')_{d'} = (T_{d'})_{D_{d*,d'}}', with stray asterisks or slips; the intended meaning is T(d,d')_{d'} = (T_{d'})_{D_{d,d'}}.
In the line 'qui, par image inverse sur D^!_{d,d'} = D^!_d ×_{D_d} D_{d'}', the last factor should be understood as D_{d,d'}.

In (195) the top-left object is P^{(I_d)}_{d'} over D^!_d, the constant scheme of d'-element subsets of I_d. The label on the arrow D^!_{d,d'} → D_{d,d'} looks like '𝔖_{d*}' in the image rather than '𝔖_{d,d'}'.
The first word of the last paragraph is 's'identifie', preceded by a crossed-out letter.
